example: I can't believe it's already December. Time flies!
origin: Its roots go back to the Latin phrase 'tempus fugit', meaning 'time flees'.

wrong_meanings.meaning: insects fly quickly through the air
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of the words, not the idiomatic one.
The idiom describes time passing fast, not deliberately wasting it.
The idiom says nothing about punctuality; it only describes how quickly time seems to pass.

explanation: 'Time flies' is said when we notice that time has passed quickly, often when we are having fun or looking back at a period of our lives.
